# Use business-case

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Build a business case for a build/buy/defer investment decision — do-nothing always included as the baseline, benefits quantified as re-runnable calculations with confidence tags, full costs (build + run + opportunity), ranges instead of false precision, and the flip-assumption named.

**Reach for it when** the user needs to justify an investment, write a business case, compare build vs buy vs defer, or get budget/sponsor approval for an initiative.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install business-case                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install business-case --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install business-case --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Product manager pack: [`--pack product-manager`](../packs/use-the-product-manager-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Write the business case for building our own feature-flag service versus buying one"
- "Should we invest two engineer-quarters in rebuilding search? I need something to take to the sponsor"
- "Compare build vs buy vs defer for the new data pipeline, with the cost of doing nothing priced"
- "I need budget approval for an observability overhaul — help me justify the spend"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "The investment's approved — now write the PRD for the ML router"
- "Pick between Kafka, Kinesis, and Pub/Sub for the approved event bus"
- "Compress this 12-page business case into a one-page summary for the board"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use business-case".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Option 0 is present and costed.** A case that doesn't price the status quo hasn't established there's a problem worth money.
- **Every benefit is a re-runnable calculation** with sourced inputs and a confidence tag. Reviewers check arithmetic; they can't check adjectives.
- **Outputs are ranges; the case says which end is likelier.** False precision fails the doc even when the direction is right.
- **All three cost layers appear per option** — build, run, opportunity — with the displaced work named, not waved at.
- **The flip-assumption is identified** and, where confidence on it is low, a de-risking step is proposed before full commitment.
- **The recommendation is singular and the runner-up's best argument is stated fairly.** A case that strawmans the alternative converts no skeptics.
- **The ask is the first thing read** — option, cost, benefit range, deadline, in under 40 words.

## Use something else when

- The investment decision is already made — go to `prd-draft`
- Choosing between technologies for an approved initiative — the investment is already decided; compare the options directly
- Compressing an existing case for execs — `exec-summary`
- Trivial cost ("should we buy a $400/yr tool") — the case costs more than the decision; just decide
